terms.gloss: cook again, melt down again: recycle
evidence: Verg. A. 7.636: recoquunt patriōs fornācibus ēnsēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Our use: Morgan–Owens has a heading recycle with no Latin, and no other reference work has a word. Classically recoquere is to boil again, or to melt down and forge again (Lewis & Short), which is what is done with glass, metal and paper. The recycling bin: excipulum recoquendōrum.
Andresian’s word for the recycling bin. Classically it occurs once, in Lucretius (5.244, Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: Don’t throw the bottle away; it’ll be recycled.

sources: Lewis & Short: recoquo · Lewis & Short: regigno
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. recycle, recycling (no Latin given).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
